title: Mandala — eight rounds
subtitle: A 30 cm wall-hanging mandala — flat-circle base, shells, V-stitches, then a picot edging
excerpt: Eight rounds give a wall-hanging mandala at 30 cm diameter. Rounds 1 to 5 work the flat-circle base; rounds 6 to 8 each introduce a new stitch texture — shells, V-stitches, then a picot edging. Blocking matters on this one: pin to a foam mat while still damp to keep the circle flat and round.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), circular motif chapter. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 1-3 (1885-1890) — the round doily construction.
heroPrompt: An eight-round crochet mandala in three colours — dusty blue, cream, and sage — on a pale wooden surface, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. The 30 cm flat circle shows concentric rounds of double crochet, shells, V-stitches, and a picot edging.

chartDefinition.title: Mandala — eight rounds
chartDefinition.caption: Eight rounds from the magic ring. Rounds 1 to 5: flat-circle double crochet with six increases per round. Round 6: treble shell groups. Round 7: V-stitch round. Round 8: picot edging.

glossaryTerms.definition: A circle that lies flat without cupping or ruffling. In crochet, a flat circle in double crochet requires six increases per round. The eight-round mandala uses five rounds of flat-circle double crochet as its base.

A V-stitch is (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr) worked into the same stitch or space. The chain-2 at the centre opens the fabric and gives the characteristic V shape. In the eight-round mandala, the V-stitch round sits between the shell round and the picot edging.
A small decorative loop formed by chaining 3 (or more), then working a slip stitch back into the first chain. Picots sit on the outer edge of lace motifs and edgings as a finishing detail.

content.text: The eight-round mandala builds to 30 cm diameter using five rounds of
flat-circle
double crochet before introducing three distinct stitch textures in the final rounds: shells in round 6,
V-stitch
groups in round 7, and a
picot
edging in round 8. This is a wall-hanging piece at 30 cm — large enough to hang as a circular panel or use as a centrepiece on a table.

Blocking matters on this one more than on the smaller mandalas. Pin to a foam mat while still damp to keep the circle flat and round — a 30 cm circle that dries unblocked will develop a gentle wave that is hard to remove afterwards. A generous steam application, then leaving flat overnight pinned at all six shell points, gives the best result.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 40 g of DK-weight cotton across one to three colours. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and plenty of blocking pins — at 30 cm you need at least 12 pins to hold the outer round flat.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished eight-round mandala measures 30 cm diameter in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after steam-blocking. Check your tension by working a five-round mandala first: if it measures 20 cm, your tension is correct for the full eight-round version.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; called single crochet (sc) in US patterns.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns.
V-stitch — (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr) in same space. UK and US term shared.
picot — ch 3, sl st into first ch. Decorative outer edging loop. UK and US term shared.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Place a stitch marker in the first stitch of each double-crochet round. Do not turn.
Round 1
Form a magic ring. Ch 1. Work 6 dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc to join. Pull tail to close ring. (6 dc.)
Round 2
Ch 1. Work 2 dc into each stitch around. Sl st to first dc to join. (12 dc.)
Round 3
Ch 1. *2 dc in next st, 1 dc in next st*; repeat from * to * five more times. Sl st to first dc to join. (18 dc.)
Round 4
Ch 1. *2 dc in next st, 1 dc in each of next 2 sts*; repeat from * to * five more times. Sl st to first dc to join. (24 dc.)
Round 5
Ch 1. *2 dc in next st, 1 dc in each of next 3 sts*; repeat from * to * five more times. Sl st to first dc to join. (30 dc.)
Round 6 — Shell round

If changing colour, fasten off round 5 yarn and join new colour. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Into same stitch work 4 tr. *Ch 2, skip 4 sts, 5 tr into next st*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (6 shells of 5 tr, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Round 7 — V-stitch round

Sl st across to first ch-2 sp. Ch 4 (counts as tr, ch 1). *Into same ch-2 sp work (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr). Ch 1. Into next ch-2 sp work (1 tr, ch 1)*; repeat from * to * four more times. Into same ch-2 sp work (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr). Ch 1. Sl st to top of beg ch-4 to join. (12 V-stitch arms, 6 ch-2 open spaces, 12 ch-1 spaces.)
Round 8 — Picot edging

If changing colour, fasten off round 7 yarn and join new colour. *Into each ch-2 sp work (1 tr, ch 3, sl st into first ch of ch-3 just made — picot formed, 1 tr). Into each ch-1 sp work (1 tr)*; repeat from * to * around all V-stitch groups. Sl st to first tr to join. Fasten off. (Picot loop at each of the 6 main ch-2 spaces; plain trebles filling the ch-1 side spaces.)
Chart

The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Rounds 1 to 5 are flat-circle double crochet; round 6 shows six shell groups; round 7 shows the V-stitch ring; round 8 shows the picot edging at the outer points.

definition.title: Mandala — eight rounds
definition.caption: Eight rounds from the magic ring. Rounds 1 to 5: flat-circle double crochet. Round 6: six 5-tr shells. Round 7: V-stitch ring. Round 8: picot edging at six outer points.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Thread through a tapestry needle and weave through 4 stitches on the wrong side, reverse direction through 3 stitches, and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail and any colour-change tails — with three colours you will have up to six tails. Block on a large foam mat: pin all six outer picot points first, then pin the midpoints of each arc between picots, then apply steam and leave flat overnight.
Joining

The eight-round mandala is best used as a standalone piece — a wall hanging, a large coaster, or the centrepiece panel of a tote bag. For a panel project, join through the ch-2 spaces at the six outer picot points using a flat slip-stitch seam, then fill the gaps between circles with a background grid of chain arches and trebles.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Do not tumble-dry. Re-block on a foam mat after each wash — at 30 cm, a damp mandala will distort slightly as it dries if left flat without pins.
What to try next

The lacy mandala (eight rounds) replaces the solid double-crochet base with open double-treble fans from round 3 onward, giving a 32 cm motif that is mostly air — a fine-gauge wall piece or table centrepiece. The five-round mandala is the same construction but stops before the V-stitch and picot rounds, which is useful if you want a smaller version without the decorative outer layers.
